c: Everyday Home, a home goods retailer with 40 stores
s: Everyday Home needs to decide how many reusable kitchen storage sets to buy for the next holiday season. A supplier offers a lower price for a large order but requires payment up front and offers no returns. Last year, a similar product sold out two weeks before the holiday.
The merchandise director (judge) wants you and your partner to analyze the choices and recommend how many to buy and from which supplier.
f: Supplier A: $11.50 each, minimum 20,000 units, no returns
Supplier B: $13.75 each, minimum 5,000 units, returns accepted
Last year: 9,000 units sold; 1,500 stolen or damaged
p: Determine quantities to buy/reorder
Evaluate vendors' goods and services
Negotiate terms with suppliers
Determine stock turnover
Determine final cost of purchases from domestic and international sources
n: Estimates demand using last year's sales and trends
Compares unit cost, minimums, return policy and risk of leftover stock
Considers warehouse space and cash flow
Suggests negotiating a split order or a return clause
Explains how turnover affects profit
q: What would you do if the product did not sell by January?
Which supplier would you choose for the first order, and what would you change next year?

s: Northside Apparel marked down its winter coats 40% in November to boost sales. Sales increased, but profit fell and the company now has a competitor offering the same coats at a similar discount.
The vice president (judge) wants you and your partner to recommend a pricing strategy for next winter that protects margins and keeps customers.
f: Sales rose 55% but gross profit dollars fell 12%
15% of customers buy only on sale
p: Explain factors affecting pricing decisions
Describe the role of business ethics in pricing
Explain legal considerations for pricing
Identify product opportunities
Explain the nature of sales forecasts
n: Calculates margin at full price and discounted price
Discusses customer price sensitivity and competitor pricing
Warns against misleading 'original price' claims
Suggests alternatives: bundles, loyalty perks, limited-time offers
Uses forecasts to plan inventory and markdown timing
q: How would you decide when to mark down an item and by how much?
What are the risks of training customers to wait for sales?

c: Zest Beverages, a maker of sparkling water
s: Zest Beverages sells through grocery stores, convenience stores and its own website. Grocery stores want exclusive flavors, while the website customers want subscription delivery. Shipping costs are rising and some retailers are complaining about online discounts.
The vice president (judge) wants you and your partner to recommend how to manage the distribution channels and keep retailers happy.
f: Two grocery chains threaten to drop the brand
p: Explain the nature of channel-member relationships
Explain the nature of channels of distribution
Coordinate channel management with other marketing activities
Describe ethical considerations in channel management
Explain legal considerations in channel management
n: Describes how conflict arises when a producer sells direct and through retailers
Suggests exclusive flavors, fair pricing and clear communication
Coordinates promotion and inventory across channels
Treats retailers fairly and honors agreements
Notes price discrimination and exclusivity rules
q: Should Zest raise online prices to match stores? Why?
How would you rebuild trust with a retailer who feels undercut?

c: Shoreline Outfitters, an online retailer of outdoor clothing
s: Shoreline Outfitters' return rate is 28%, mostly because of sizing. Customers also complain that return shipping is slow and refunds take two weeks. Return costs are cutting into profit.
The CEO (judge) wants you and your partner to recommend how to reduce returns and improve the customer experience without losing sales.
f: Top reason for returns: size or fit (62%)
p: Describe the use of technology in customer relationship management
Interpret business policies to customers/clients
Handle customer/client complaints
Build and maintain relationships with customers
Explain the role of customer service as a component of selling relationships
n: Suggests size guides, fit tools, reviews and customer photos
Faster refunds, clear policies and prepaid labels
Collects and analyzes return reasons
Responds to complaints with empathy and a fix
Balances cost of returns with lifetime value of customers
q: Would you charge for returns? Why or why not?
How would you reward customers who keep their purchases?

s: Metro Mart collects data from its loyalty program but has not used it. Executives want to reduce waste in promotions and discover which customers are likely to stop shopping.
The marketing director (judge) wants you and your partner to propose how the company should analyze its data and what actions it should take.
f: 40% shop less than twice per year
p: Apply marketing analytics
Leverage data to recommend personalized, relevant campaigns
Interpret statistical findings
Maintain security of marketing data
Explain ethical considerations in providing information
n: Segments customers by frequency, spending and product categories
Targets mailers and offers by segment
Looks at trends and tests changes before rolling out
Protects data and follows privacy rules
Is open about how data is used and offers opt-outs
q: How would you test whether personalized offers work better than the mailers?
Would you share customer data with a partner company? Why or why not?
